author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Left-context compaction filters long tokens before applying the legacy 40-character budget.
findings.consequence: Nuxt can display extra leading left-context words that Angular would have dropped, changing search-result row text and width for highlights that contain a 30+ character token before the match.
findings.evidence: The owned unit first creates `compacted` by removing tokens with `word.length >= 30` on line 729, then computes and applies the 40-character budget to that shortened list. The legacy implementation in `../app/scripts/services.js` computes `num_chars` over the original `left_context`, splices leading tokens when `num_chars > 40`, and only afterwards filters both contexts through `isShort`. For `[20-char short, 30-char long, 10-char tail]`, legacy returns only the 10-char tail after the long token is filtered, while this function returns both the 20-char token and the tail; the current unit test at `test/unit/text-search.spec.ts:1129` encodes the Nuxt behavior rather than the legacy behavior.
findings.recommendation: Preserve Angular order without mutation: compute the character budget over the original `context`, choose the slice start from that original list, then return `context.slice(start).filter(token => token.word.length < 30)`. Update the unit case that currently expects discarded long words to be excluded before budgeting.
